free_sources: AP Top 25 voter ballots published on apnews.com (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for archive depth and bulk access)
cbb.ap_voter_ballot_panel.label: AP voter ballot panel: individual ballots and update rules
cbb.ap_voter_ballot_panel.measurement: Collect each weekly ballot (voter id, ranks 1 to 25); for each voter-team-week compute rank change as a function of the team's result (win/loss, opponent rank, margin, site), prior rank and a voter fixed effect; fit a mixed model with voter random slopes using 5 seasons; simulate the poll as the sum of voter points from the fitted update rules (25 points for 1st down to 1 for 25th); as-of: previous poll plus results.
cbb.ap_voter_ballot_panel.mechanism: The AP poll aggregates individual ballots published by voter; each voter's update after results has its own inertia and preferences, so the aggregate response to a loss is the sum of heterogeneous responses.
cbb.ap_voter_ballot_panel.rationale: A voter-level model captures both the average reaction to a loss and the dispersion that makes top-two ties or leapfrogs likely; aggregate-only models cannot tell whether a swing is a few extreme voters or broad movement.

free_sources: Sports-Reference team and player assist stats
cbb.assist_conversion_chain.label: Assist chain: potential assists times assisted share of teammates' shots
cbb.assist_conversion_chain.measurement: expected team assisted FGM = sum_z FGA_z * make_z * assisted_share_z (opponent-adjusted, last 15 games with shrinkage n/(n+10)); player assists = creation_share_i (assists per team assisted FGM while on floor, last 2 seasons, shrunk to role mean with n/(n+600 minutes)) * team assisted FGM * (minutes_i/40) * on-floor adjustment for lineup partners; as-of: prior games and scenario weighting.
cbb.assist_conversion_chain.mechanism: Expected assists equal the player's share of team creation times the expected number of team assisted field goals, which depends on the mix of shot types (threes and dunks are mostly assisted, post-ups and isolations rarely).
cbb.assist_conversion_chain.rationale: The assist line moves with the team's expected assisted made baskets, a quantity forecastable from shot mix and shot-quality, not from the player's own assist average; scorer discretion adds a venue term.
raw_data: team assisted and unassisted FGM by shot type

cbb.assisted_three_dependency.label: Share of a shooter's threes that are assisted, and by whom
cbb.assisted_three_dependency.measurement: For each shooter compute assisted_share = assisted 3PM / total 3PM and assister distribution over the last 2 seasons with shrinkage n/(n+40 makes); with/without effect: delta attempts per 40 and delta make rate when the top assister is off the floor (ridge shrinkage lambda = 150 minutes off); expected scenario shift = sum_k P(creator_k out) * delta_k; as-of: prior games.
cbb.assisted_three_dependency.mechanism: A spot-up shooter's attempts and quality depend on one or two creators supplying catch-and-shoot passes, so the loss of that creator reduces both attempts and open-look quality.
cbb.assisted_three_dependency.rationale: Assisted share varies from about 40 percent for creators to over 90 percent for stationary shooters; teammate absence shifts for creators raise the shooter's off-dribble attempts at lower quality while shooters' catch-and-shoot attempts fall, so the sign depends on dependence.

free_sources: Sports-Reference award and all-conference pages (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for voting totals)
Bart Torvik player tables (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for history)
cbb.award_candidate_profile.label: Award candidate profile: production, team success and voter-criteria features by award type
cbb.award_candidate_profile.measurement: For each award type separately, fit a conditional (multinomial) logit across candidates within each past award-season: features are team AdjEM_fund rank and win percentage, player BPM or Torvik PRPG rank, points, rebounds, assists, steals plus blocks per game, defensive rating or block/steal rates (Defensive Player of the Year only), class (freshman or newcomer indicator for those awards), previous all-conference selection, preseason watch-list membership; train on all available seasons per award (at least 10 where history exists, otherwise pool with an award-type indicator), as-of the last games before voting closes; output candidate shares, then split payout probability for ties (1/N rule).
cbb.award_candidate_profile.mechanism: Award voters (national media panels, conference coaches or media) pick from candidates by scoring and overall production, team success, role-specific criteria (defence for Defensive Player of the Year, class for freshman honours) and narrative; a per-award choice model on those features gives the winner distribution.
cbb.award_candidate_profile.rationale: The record's award stage had only cbb.news and a usage rate, which cannot separate candidates for conference awards such as Defensive Player of the Year or Newcomer awards whose criteria differ from player of the year. Voter bodies and criteria differ by award, so one pooled model is wrong.
raw_data: award winners and finalists by award and season
player season statistics and advanced ratings
team results and ratings at voting close

cbb.award_selection_model.label: Award selection model: candidate sets, team success dependence and co-recipient probability
cbb.award_selection_model.measurement: For MOP: P(player) = sum over teams of P(team champion) * share_player|champion, where share is a multinomial logit on Final Four box-score points per game and star flags fitted to 1990 to 2026 MOP history (champion-conditioned) plus a 3 to 6 percent chance MOP comes from a non-champion; for POY and conference awards: multinomial logit among candidates on BPM, points per game, team rank and conference record, with year-specific fixed effects; co-recipient rate from history (about 1 to 3 percent for major awards); expected payout = P(win) * E[1/N]; as-of: vote deadline and latest stats.
cbb.award_selection_model.mechanism: Award winners come from a candidate set defined by performance and team success; the Most Outstanding Player depends on the champion, while Player of the Year awards weigh production, team rank and narrative.
cbb.award_selection_model.rationale: Three contract families (tournament MOP, national player of the year, conference awards) have different drivers; treating them all as 'production' misses that MOP is mostly a title contract, and a 1/N split changes the expected payout.
raw_data: player season statistics and team rank at vote time

cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.label: Ball-handler succession: who inherits creation when the primary handler is out
cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.measurement: From with/without data over the last two seasons, for each team compute the change in assists per 40 for each rotation player when the primary handler (highest assist share) is off the floor, shrinking with n/(n+250 minutes) to a role-mean redistribution (such as 55 percent to the next guard, 25 percent to wings, 20 percent lost); output the redistribution vector; as-of: prior games.
cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.mechanism: When a primary creator is absent, assists redistribute to the next handler in a team-specific order and a share of creation is lost because the replacement creates less efficiently.
cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.rationale: Teammate absence shifts are not symmetric across the roster; some teams have a clear second handler, others spread creation, which changes the sign of the replacement's assist line and the team's total assists.
raw_data: on/off possession and assist data by player

free_sources: Bart Torvik player and lineup tables (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)
cbb.bench_unit_efficiency.label: Bench-unit and garbage-time-unit offensive efficiency
cbb.bench_unit_efficiency.measurement: From lineup data compute points per 100 possessions for lineups with at most 2 of the top-6 minutes players, over the last two seasons, shrunk to the team's starters-unit rating with weight n/(n+400 possessions) and to a league bench mean; stored with the share of team minutes played by such units when the team led by 15 or more (blowout minutes share). As-of: prior games.
cbb.bench_unit_efficiency.mechanism: Points per possession of units outside the top rotation (minutes below the top-6) is lower than the starters', and determines the favourite's scoring after starters sit.
cbb.bench_unit_efficiency.rationale: In lopsided games the final 8 to 10 minutes are played by non-starters; team total at a high strike for a favourite depends on the efficiency of those units, which differs widely between deep programmes and thin ones.

cbb.bracket_seed_statistic_sim.label: Per-simulation bracket seed statistics (upset counts, #k-seed counts by round, semifinal seed sum, maximum upset seed margin)
cbb.bracket_seed_statistic_sim.measurement: From cbb.bracket_sim (100,000 tournaments using current ratings with posterior sd, bracket as published or simulated seeds before Selection Sunday): per simulation compute (a) for each round r and seed k, number of #k seeds reaching r and winning in r; (b) number of games in round r won by the higher numerical seed; (c) sum of official seeds of the four semifinalists; (d) max over all games of (winner seed - loser seed) where positive, with and without First Four games; (e) for each round r, the highest numerical seed reaching r (title-only KXMARMADHIGHSEED). Output the pmf of each statistic; calibrate to 1985-present seed-level history via a check of mean counts.
cbb.bracket_seed_statistic_sim.mechanism: Bracket-wide seed contracts settle on deterministic functions of all games' outcomes, so their probabilities are the empirical distributions of those functions over simulated tournaments.
cbb.bracket_seed_statistic_sim.rationale: These statistics aggregate dependent games: an early upset removes a favourite and changes later matchups, and year-specific seed-line strength gaps shift all counts together. Historical seed base rates alone ignore the current field; per-team advancement probabilities alone cannot give counts or maxima because they lose the joint structure.
raw_data: published bracket with seeds and First Four pairings
historical tournament game results with both seeds and round
team ratings with posterior sd at pricing

cbb.candidate_availability_calendar.label: Candidate availability calendar: current-team season status, buyout step-downs and pro-league timing
cbb.candidate_availability_calendar.measurement: Per candidate as of t: current team's elimination status and earliest elimination date (from bracket simulation), buyout step-down dates and amounts, NBA team playoff status for NBA assistants; per school: transfer-portal opening date and days remaining; feature = expected days until candidate is free versus expected days until school wants a hire.
cbb.candidate_availability_calendar.mechanism: A candidate coaching a team still alive in the NCAA tournament, an NBA assistant in the playoffs, or one whose buyout drops on a set date is effectively unavailable until that event passes.
cbb.candidate_availability_calendar.rationale: Searches either wait for a preferred candidate or move on; this changes both who is hired and when. Subtle: transfer-portal windows push schools to hire before the portal opens, which penalises candidates whose teams advance deep in March.

free_sources: NCAA Legislative Services infractions decisions database
cbb.candidate_eligibility_constraints.label: Candidate eligibility constraints: NCAA show-cause orders, pending infractions and legal or conduct issues
cbb.candidate_eligibility_constraints.measurement: Per candidate: active NCAA show-cause (start, end, restrictions) from NCAA infractions decisions database; open infractions case flag; public conduct investigations; binary 'constrained at t' and days until constraint lapses.
cbb.candidate_eligibility_constraints.mechanism: A show-cause penalty, pending infractions case or conduct investigation makes most schools unwilling or unable to hire a candidate during its term.
cbb.candidate_eligibility_constraints.rationale: This removes names that a pure track-record ranking would rate highly. Subtle: show-cause orders allow hiring with restrictions, and some schools accept the restrictions; the term end date matters relative to the cutoff.
raw_data: infractions decisions: person, penalty, start/end dates

free_sources: Wikipedia coach and AD career pages
cbb.candidate_program_ties.label: Candidate ties to the programme, athletic director and conference region
cbb.candidate_program_ties.measurement: Binary and count features per candidate-school pair: alumnus (played/graduated), former staff member (years, role), previous hire or colleague of the current AD (matched through AD career history), same agent as other staff, head-coaching job within 500 miles or in the same conference footprint; computed from public biographies as of t.
cbb.candidate_program_ties.mechanism: Hires disproportionately go to coaches with prior links: alumni, former assistants of the programme, previous hires of the same AD, coaches already in the region or recruiting footprint.
cbb.candidate_program_ties.rationale: Ties lower information and negotiation costs and are a strong prior over candidate identity; they also explain why a less-accomplished candidate may beat a better record. Subtle: the AD's own career history (schools worked at, previous coaching hires) is often more predictive than the candidate's ties to the school itself.
raw_data: AD career history and list of prior coaching hires

cbb.clinch_and_elimination_effort_shift.label: Effort and rotation change after clinching or elimination from title races
cbb.clinch_and_elimination_effort_shift.measurement: Define stakes_i,g = |dP(top4 finish)/d(win this game)| from the standings simulation and the bubble/seed leverage from the resume model; regress game margin residuals (actual minus rating-implied) on stakes_i - stakes_j and a clinch flag using 8 seasons of the final 6 conference games; expected effect 0.5 to 1.5 points (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED); as-of: standings before each game.
cbb.clinch_and_elimination_effort_shift.mechanism: Teams that have clinched a seed or title, or are out of any race, may rest starters or alter intensity in the last games, which shifts win probabilities against the pure strength gap.
cbb.clinch_and_elimination_effort_shift.rationale: Top-N and win-total contracts include the last two weeks of the conference season in which stakes differ across teams; an incentive-blind model overstates the win probability of clinched teams and understates that of teams chasing a bid or a top-four double bye.
raw_data: seed and bid leverage computed by simulation

free_sources: conference websites (championship policy, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for every league)
cbb.co_champion_expected_share.label: Expected 1/N share of a conference regular-season title
cbb.co_champion_expected_share.measurement: From the joint standings simulation (cbb.conference_standings_sim, 50,000 seasons, remaining conference games only, completed results fixed as of pricing): for each simulated season let W* = best conference win-loss record and T = set of teams with that record; if the league's policy is to declare co-champions, team i's share = 1{i in T}/|T|; if it names one champion by tiebreak, share = 1{i is tiebreak winner}. Expected share = mean over simulations. Policy flag per conference from published championship policy, versioned by season.
cbb.co_champion_expected_share.mechanism: A declared co-championship splits the payout, so the value of a regular-season champion contract is the expected share, determined by how often the team ties for first and with how many others.
cbb.co_champion_expected_share.rationale: Pricing the champion series as P(best record) or P(wins tiebreak) is wrong under a 1/N rule: a team that often ties for first with one rival is worth about half of its tie probability. The size of the error grows in balanced leagues where two- and three-way ties at the top are common.
raw_data: historical counts of co-champions by league

free_sources: Naismith Awards website (winners, finalists; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED history)
preseason conference polls on conference websites
cbb.coach_award_profile.label: Coach-of-the-year candidate profile: over-performance versus preseason expectation
cbb.coach_award_profile.measurement: Per coach-season as of pricing: (actual win% - preseason projected win%) from preseason ratings, (preseason AP rank - current AP rank, unranked = 35), conference finish versus preseason conference poll, first-year flag, projected end-of-season values from the season simulation. Fit a multinomial logit on past Naismith/AP COTY winners and finalists (2000-present) with these features; output P(win) per coach, renormalised over active candidates.
cbb.coach_award_profile.mechanism: Coach awards are voted on how far a team outperforms what was expected of it, so the driver is the gap between realised and preseason-expected success, not team strength itself.
cbb.coach_award_profile.rationale: A model using team strength would pick coaches of the best teams, who rarely win; the award follows over-performance (wins and AP rank versus preseason poll and projection), conference titles and tournament runs, with recency weighting toward February and March. Some voters favour first-year turnarounds. This is distinct from player award profiles.
raw_data: past COTY winners and finalists by year
preseason projections and final records by team

cbb.coach_blowout_substitution_rate.label: Coach-specific bench-clearing and lead-protection behaviour
cbb.coach_blowout_substitution_rate.measurement: From play-by-play: for every game in which a team led by at least 15 at any media timeout, compute lead_at_time_t (t = 12:00, 8:00, 4:00 remaining) and the final margin; coach_decay = mean(final_margin - lead_at_8min) per 8 minutes of game time, estimated over the coach's last 4 seasons with shrinkage weight n/(n+15) to the league mean decay, split by lead bucket (15 to 25, over 25). Also compute the share of second-half minutes played by the top-5 minutes players when ahead by 20 or more.
cbb.coach_blowout_substitution_rate.mechanism: How quickly a coach removes starters and what pace he plays once ahead by a lot determines how much of an in-game lead survives to the final margin.
cbb.coach_blowout_substitution_rate.rationale: Cover probability at large spreads is dominated by the end-of-game margin decay, not by the pregame mean. Some coaches play starters until a 30-point lead; others empty the bench at +20 by the second-half under-12 timeout. This is a stable trait across seasons (coach, not roster), unlike team scoring luck.
raw_data: play-by-play with game clock and score

free_sources: Knight Commission / USA Today athletic finance database
cbb.coach_candidate_track_record.label: Head-coach candidate track record, opponent-adjusted and resource-adjusted
cbb.coach_candidate_track_record.measurement: For each candidate: seasons as head coach; mean change in adjusted efficiency margin (point-in-time end-of-season Torvik/KenPom) versus the three seasons before arrival; NCAA bids, tournament wins and Sweet 16s in last 5 seasons; resource-adjusted margin = residual of adjusted margin on conference and athletic budget; for assistants: years as top assistant and head-coach tree; shrink single-season effects with weight n/(n+3) seasons.
cbb.coach_candidate_track_record.mechanism: Hiring committees choose among candidates largely on demonstrated programme-building: rating improvement over predecessor, tournament results, recruiting/portal success and conduct record.
cbb.coach_candidate_track_record.rationale: A candidate's raw win-loss record mixes coaching value with programme resources; schools ranking candidates (and reporters naming them) favour coaches whose teams outperform their budget and conference. Subtle: one deep NCAA run inflates perceived value far more than multi-year efficiency gains, so both should be measured.
raw_data: coach career table: coach, school, season, role, W-L, tournament result
end-of-season adjusted efficiency margin by team-season

cbb.coach_early_foul_bench_rule.label: Coach policy: benching players with early fouls in the first half
cbb.coach_early_foul_bench_rule.measurement: From play-by-play, for each coach (last 3 seasons) take all starter instances with 2 fouls before the 8:00 mark of the first half; compute P(sit within 2 minutes of the 2nd foul) and the mean minutes missed until return, shrinking each to the league mean with weight n/(n+8); combine with the player's per-minute foul rate (opponent-adjusted) to give expected first-half minutes lost = sum over starters P(2 fouls by time t)*P(sit)*mean_minutes_missed. As-of: through prior game.
cbb.coach_early_foul_bench_rule.mechanism: The loss of minutes from early fouls depends on whether the coach sits a starter after two fouls before the break and for how long.
cbb.coach_early_foul_bench_rule.rationale: Foul rates are stable, but minute loss is a coach decision: some coaches always sit at two fouls, others only after three or when the lead is large. Without this, 'foul trouble risk' is only half a mechanism.
raw_data: play-by-play foul events with player id and clock

free_sources: Historical search coverage (ESPN, CBS) reconstructed by date
cbb.coach_hire_field_residual.label: Residual probability mass for unlisted candidates and for no permanent hire by the cutoff
cbb.coach_hire_field_residual.measurement: From past searches: fraction of hires that were not among the first N publicly linked names at days d since the SEARCH opened (d = 0, 7, 14, 30; the clock is held at 0 until the announced search start, using search_start_lag from the vacancy-state input), estimated as a curve with binomial confidence bands; no-hire mass = P(no vacancy exists by the cutoff, from the incumbent hazard input) + P(search not concluding by Sep 1, 2027 given its start date) + probability that the interim is made permanent (counted for the interim's own market, not for the residual) or that only an interim or coach-in-waiting is named; as-of t.
cbb.coach_hire_field_residual.mechanism: The multi-outcome contract lists named candidates only; the true distribution includes an 'other' mass (a candidate not listed) and a 'no permanent hire before deadline' mass.
cbb.coach_hire_field_residual.rationale: Listed-candidate probabilities must sum to at most 1 minus these masses; historically many hires are names that were not among the earliest-reported candidates. Subtle: the 'other' mass shrinks quickly as the search progresses and reports concentrate, so it is time-varying.
raw_data: per past search: opening date, candidate link dates, hire identity and date

cbb.coach_vacancy_search_state.label: Coaching vacancy search state: opening date, decision-makers, search firm and interim arrangement
cbb.coach_vacancy_search_state.measurement: Per vacancy, as-of timestamp t: opening date and cause (fired, resigned, retired, left for another job), announced search start date or rule ('begins after the season', 'immediately', none stated), search_start_lag = announced search start minus opening date in days, days since the SEARCH opened (floored at 0 while the school says the search has not begun; this, not days since the vacancy, indexes every conversion and residual curve), whether an interim is named, who, and for what span (rest of season or until a hire), AD tenure in years, search firm named (yes/no, which firm), count of publicly reported interviewed candidates and finalists at t, whether a board/regent approval meeting is scheduled; each field carries the first public report timestamp, never backfilled.
cbb.coach_vacancy_search_state.mechanism: A hire is the end of a search process run by an athletic director, sometimes a president or board and often a search firm; how far the search has progressed bounds both timing and candidate set.
cbb.coach_vacancy_search_state.rationale: Searches opened by a firing late in a season move fast and usually finish within weeks, but a retirement announced just before a season can be followed by a deliberately deferred search while an interim coaches the whole season; in that regime days since the vacancy carry almost no information and the interim's season does. Subtle: a school can announce the search start in the opening press release, and that single field decides which timing regime applies; the stage of the search (interviews reported, finalist count) then shifts probability between named and unnamed candidates.
raw_data: vacancy table: school, opening_date, cause, interim_coach, interim_span, announced_search_start, AD_name, AD_start_date, search_firm, board_meeting_dates
report log: timestamp, outlet, candidate, stage (contacted/interviewed/finalist/offer)

free_sources: ESPN, CBS Sports and The Athletic reporting
X/Twitter posts of national insiders (capture timestamps)
cbb.coaching_search_report_ledger.label: Timestamped coaching-search report ledger with source reliability and report-to-hire conversion
cbb.coaching_search_report_ledger.measurement: Log every public report with timestamp (UTC), outlet and reporter, candidate, stage in {linked, contacted, interviewed, finalist, offer, agreement, denial}; estimate historical conversion P(hired | stage, outlet tier) from past D1 power-conference searches (at least 5 cycles), shrunk toward stage mean with weight n/(n+10); denial reports from the candidate tracked separately with their own conversion rate.
cbb.coaching_search_report_ledger.mechanism: Insider reports (interviewed, finalist, offer, agreement in principle) are noisy but increasingly informative signals; their historical conversion to actual hires depends on outlet, report stage and lead time.
cbb.coaching_search_report_ledger.rationale: Most of the information about a search arrives as reports, and a single credible agreement report moves the outcome near certainty; but early lists of names include many that never had serious contact. Subtle: candidates and agents leak interest to gain leverage at their current school, so 'interest' reports convert far less than 'finalist' or 'offer' reports.
raw_data: report log: ts, outlet, reporter, candidate, stage, link

cbb.committee_availability_treatment.label: Seed adjustment for key players missing at Selection Sunday
cbb.committee_availability_treatment.measurement: From past years list teams with a rotation player (top 3 by minutes or BPM) out at Selection Sunday, compute seed residual from the revealed-preference model, estimate the mean residual by player importance (BPM share) with a prior mean of -0.5 lines and a sd of 1.0, shrinking by n/(n+10); as-of: injury status published before Selection Sunday.
cbb.committee_availability_treatment.mechanism: The committee takes player availability into account in some way, so a team missing a star may be placed lower (or protected) than metrics alone imply.
cbb.committee_availability_treatment.rationale: An injury late in the season changes how good the team is without changing its resume; whether the committee seeds on full-strength or current-strength is a discrete, partially discretionary choice with a few lines at stake.
raw_data: injury list at Selection Sunday per team per year

free_sources: NCAA.com NET archive and team sheets
cbb.committee_metric_revealed_weights.label: Revealed committee weights on NET, WAB, SOR, quadrant record and predictive ratings by seed range
cbb.committee_metric_revealed_weights.measurement: For seasons 2018 to 2026 (post-NET) fit an ordered probit for final seed (1 to 16, plus missed) on standardised NET rank, WAB, SOR, KPI, KenPom rank, Q1 wins, Q3+Q4 losses and conference tournament result, with weights allowed to vary in three seed bands (1-4, 5-10, 11-16 and bubble) via interaction terms; regularise with ridge; output coefficient vector with standard errors and the committee noise sd; as-of: metrics at Selection Sunday and weekly in March.
cbb.committee_metric_revealed_weights.mechanism: The committee's ranking behaves like a latent score over the metrics with weights that differ at the top of the field and on the bubble.
cbb.committee_metric_revealed_weights.rationale: Using KenPom or NET alone ranks teams as an analyst would, not as the committee did; an ordered-probit fit on past seeds reveals that, for instance, quality wins count more at the top and bad losses more on the bubble.
raw_data: final seeds and field per year
metric values at Selection Sunday per team per year

free_sources: NCAA NET rankings and team sheets (ncaa.com; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for scrape access and history)
Warren Nolan (warrennolan.com) NET, quadrant records and SOS (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for archived sheets)
cbb.committee_ordinal_seed_model.label: Committee ordinal seed-line model from resume metrics and fundamentals ratings (no bracketology consensus)
cbb.committee_ordinal_seed_model.measurement: Ordered logit (cutpoints for seed lines 1 to 16 plus 'not in field') of final seed on NET rank, Quad 1 wins, Quad 3 and Quad 4 losses, WAB, SOR, last-10 record, conference-champion indicator and AdjEM_fund (cbb.ratings_fundamentals), fitted on Selection Sunday team sheets from 2018-19 (the first NET season) through the latest season, excluding the cancelled 2020 tournament, with leave-one-season-out validation and a protocol-vintage indicator for rule changes; to project before Selection Sunday, simulate remaining regular-season and conference-tournament games with the ratings model and re-evaluate the metrics per simulation; no Bracket Matrix or sportsbook input.
cbb.committee_ordinal_seed_model.mechanism: The selection committee assigns seed lines by ranking teams on results-based team-sheet metrics and consulted predictive ratings; an ordered model fitted to past committee outputs reproduces that ranking without using any outside forecast of it.
cbb.committee_ordinal_seed_model.rationale: The catalog input cbb.committee_seed_model blends an ordinal model with the Bracket Matrix consensus, which is an expert forecast and therefore a benchmark. Seed and field-membership contracts need the market-free and expert-free model so its edge over consensus can be measured.
raw_data: Selection Sunday team sheets by team and season (NET, quadrant records, WAB, SOR)
final seed lines and field membership by season

cbb.committee_protocol_vintage.label: Committee protocol vintage: metrics used, quadrant definitions, field size and bracketing rules
cbb.committee_protocol_vintage.measurement: Maintain a per-season record: metrics on team sheet, quadrant thresholds for home, neutral and away games, number of at-large and automatic bids, play-in structure, bracketing principle changes; indicator variables for protocol changes and a protocol-vintage weight for each historical season (1.0 for current protocol, 0.5 for one prior change, 0.25 for earlier) used in the fits; as-of: NCAA announcement dates.
cbb.committee_protocol_vintage.mechanism: The metrics on the team sheet, the quadrant thresholds, the number of bids and the bracketing rules change from year to year, shifting the relevant weights.
cbb.committee_protocol_vintage.rationale: Quadrant definitions and metric lists have been revised (for example the addition of WAB, adjustments to quadrant thresholds) and the field size may change for 2027 (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED); a model fit on earlier years can be mis-specified for the current protocol.

free_sources: Barttorvik (barttorvik.com: T-Rank team tables, player tables, game logs; free, scrape politely)
cbbdata API / cbbdata R package (Barttorvik-derived data, free API key)
Massey Ratings (masseyratings.com, free ratings and comparison tables)
cbb.conf_strength.label: Conference strength and cross-conference calibration
cbb.conf_strength.measurement: Hierarchical rating model with conference random effect; offset uncertainty from non-conference game counts; compare to market-implied conference strength.
cbb.conf_strength.mechanism: Cross-conference games anchor ratings across conferences; conference-level strength shapes bids, seeds and the relative value of in-conference ratings.
cbb.conf_strength.rationale: Ratings within a conference are well-identified but conference-to-conference offsets rest on a limited set of non-conference games, so conference strength has uncertainty that propagates to futures. Subtle: the bubble is sensitive to this uncertainty.

free_sources: conference tournament handbooks and championship manuals on conference websites (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED availability for all leagues)
cbb.conf_tiebreak_seeding_rules.label: Conference tiebreak procedure used to seed the conference tournament
cbb.conf_tiebreak_seeding_rules.measurement: Per conference-season, encode the ordered tiebreak steps as a function over simulated final standings: step list (head-to-head record among tied teams, record against teams in seeding order, NET rank on a stated date, coin flip). Apply to each simulated season from cbb.conference_standings_sim to assign seeds 1..n before simulating the tournament bracket. Versioned by publication date; unspecified steps fall back to NET rank.
cbb.conf_tiebreak_seeding_rules.mechanism: Tied teams are ordered for tournament seeding by the league's published procedure (head-to-head, record versus the top of the standings, NET), which decides byes, campus hosting and bracket side.
cbb.conf_tiebreak_seeding_rules.rationale: REGTOP settlement ignores tiebreaks, but tournament champion and championship-game series depend on seeding: a tie for 4th decides who gets a double bye in a 15-team league, and a tie for 1st decides bracket sides for the two favourites. Ignoring the procedure assigns byes at random and misprices teams near seed-line boundaries.
raw_data: per-conference tiebreak step lists by season

cbb.conf_tournament_format_table.label: Conference tournament format table for 2026-27 (size, byes, hosting, seeding, tiebreakers)
cbb.conf_tournament_format_table.measurement: Maintain a table with fields: league, teams in field, rounds, byes by seed, hosting rule (neutral, campus, higher-seed), venue city, dates, tiebreaker order for regular-season seeding, auto-bid flag; simulate the league bracket from the current standings projection using the model's pairwise win probability with a home adjustment of 3.5 points where the format hosts; refresh when conferences announce changes (realignment, new members) before each season; as-of: announcement date.
cbb.conf_tournament_format_table.mechanism: Each league has its own bracket: number of participants, byes for top seeds, campus versus neutral venue, reseeding, tiebreakers that set seeds, and days of rest between games.
cbb.conf_tournament_format_table.rationale: More than thirty ledger series settle on a conference tournament; probability for the top seed varies by format as much as by rating (a top seed with a double bye needs three wins in a 14-team field, a four-team Ivy field needs two), and some formats let the higher seed host.

cbb.crash_vs_get_back_scheme.label: Offensive-rebounding crash rate versus transition-defence tradeoff by team
cbb.crash_vs_get_back_scheme.measurement: For each team compute ORB% (offensive rebounds per available) and opponent transition points per 100 over the last 20 games with half-life 10, shrunk n/(n+10) to the league mean; expected game ORB% for the pair = league mean + 0.5*(crash_A_offense_z + crash_B_defense_allow_z) in standard deviation units of 3.5 points; as-of: prior games.
cbb.crash_vs_get_back_scheme.mechanism: Some coaches send multiple players to the offensive glass, which raises offensive rebounds for the crashers and lowers the opponent's defensive-rebound count, while others retreat to prevent transition scoring.
cbb.crash_vs_get_back_scheme.rationale: Offensive rebound totals for a big are partly a scheme choice; a high-crash team facing a low-crash opponent offers more rebounds to every big than their per-minute averages from other matchups.
raw_data: team ORB% and DRB% by game

cbb.d3_team_rating.label: Division III team rating (margin-based, opponent- and venue-adjusted)
cbb.d3_team_rating.measurement: Ridge-regressed least-squares margin rating on all D3-vs-D3 games of the current season up to the as-of time: margin_ij = r_i - r_j + h*home_ij + e, home term h fitted per season (prior 3.0 pts, sd 1.5), game weight exp(-days/60), ridge penalty equivalent to 8 games at the prior mean. Prior mean r_i = 0.55 * last season's final rating, reverted to conference mean. Margins capped at 25 to limit blowout leverage. Win probability = Phi(gap / 11). Units: points per game; snapshot stored daily with as-of timestamp, using only games final before pricing.
cbb.d3_team_rating.mechanism: A Division III game margin is generated by the same possession process as a D1 game, but neither team appears in D1 rating systems, so the strength gap must come from a rating fitted on the D3 schedule graph.
cbb.d3_team_rating.rationale: KXNCAAMBD3GAME lists D3 games (the sampled market is the DIII national final). D1 ratings, tier priors and the D1 home-court constant do not apply; D3 rosters change each year with no portal-scale data, and late-season D3 tournament games are often at campus sites, so venue must be modelled explicitly. Without this input the archetype has no strength term for a whole series.
raw_data: D3 game results: date, home team, away team, neutral flag, final score

cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.label: Cause-specific non-appearance probabilities (injury, coach decision, eligibility, suspension)
cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.measurement: Classify historical non-appearances of rotation players (top-8 minutes) into causes using news and box score patterns; estimate P(appear) = 1 - sum_c P(cause_c | status label, days since status, program type) with Beta priors by cause (for example injury questionable: 0.55 play; undisclosed: 0.97 play) updated weekly; as-of: status vintage; output also restricted-minutes probability after return (minutes cap 20 in first game back).
cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.mechanism: Different causes of absence have different base rates, different warning signals and different timing, so a single status probability mixes unlike events.
cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.rationale: College players miss games for reasons that never appear in an injury list (coach's decision, academic or eligibility issues, return from injury minutes limits); treating all absences alike loses the signal that a long-listed injury is more informative than a quiet scratch.

cbb.elimination_game_star_minutes.label: Star minutes ceiling in single-elimination tournament games
cbb.elimination_game_star_minutes.measurement: From the last 10 tournaments: for each team's top two usage players, minutes distribution in tournament games versus their own regular-season distribution, split by final margin bucket (0-5, 6-12, 13+); estimate shift in mean and in P(minutes >= 38); apply per candidate via role and coach rotation length.
cbb.elimination_game_star_minutes.mechanism: In elimination games coaches shorten rotations and play stars close to the full 40 minutes in close games, while lopsided first-round games cut star minutes.
cbb.elimination_game_star_minutes.rationale: Milestones need volume; a star's minutes distribution in the tournament differs from the regular season, with more 38+ minute games in close contests and longer media timeouts in televised tournament games giving extra rest. Subtle: overtime adds five minutes at a time and appears more often in close tournament games.

cbb.endgame_tie_decision_policy.label: Coach end-game decision policy when trailing by 2 or 3 or leading by 3 in the final possessions
cbb.endgame_tie_decision_policy.measurement: From play-by-play, for each coach (and pooled by tier): in possessions starting with under 35 seconds left and team trailing by 2, share of final shot attempts that are twos; when trailing by 3, share of threes versus quick twos; when leading by 3 with under 10 seconds, foul rate; shrink coach rates to the pooled rate with weight n/(n+15) situations over the last 5 seasons; convert to a tie-mass multiplier on P(margin=0 at 0:00). Because qualifying situations are only a handful per coach-season, use the tier-level pooled rate by default and let a coach deviate only when his shrunk rate differs from the pooled rate by more than two standard errors.
cbb.endgame_tie_decision_policy.mechanism: Whether a trailing team goes for the tying two or the winning three, and whether a leader up 3 fouls or defends, decides how much probability lands exactly on a tie at the buzzer.
cbb.endgame_tie_decision_policy.rationale: The tie probability at the end of regulation is not just the density of a smooth margin at zero: in close games the final possessions are strategic, and a coach who reliably plays for overtime raises the tie mass while one who plays for the win shifts it to plus or minus one. Subtle: holding for the last shot when tied converts a tied game into either a win or overtime, so possession at the tie matters.
raw_data: play-by-play: game_id, period, clock, score, team, event type, shot value, foul flag

cbb.final_ap_rank_mapping.label: Mapping from tournament outcome and pre-tournament rank to final AP rank
cbb.final_ap_rank_mapping.measurement: From 2000 to 2026 regress final AP rank on round reached (champion, runner-up, Final Four, Elite Eight, Sweet 16, earlier, missed tournament), pre-tournament AP rank, seed and margin of last game with an ordinal model; output P(final rank = k | round reached, pre rank) with noise sd about 1.5 places; combine with bracket_sim round-reached probabilities by Monte Carlo; as-of: bracket release, updated per round.
cbb.final_ap_rank_mapping.mechanism: The Final poll orders teams by tournament success first and pre-tournament rank second, with the champion typically placed first or near first.
cbb.final_ap_rank_mapping.rationale: A final-rank contract equals the probability of a bracket outcome mapped through the ordering rule; without the mapping, a top 10 contract would be priced as a rank persistence question, which is wrong because many pre-tournament top-10 teams lose early and fall out.

cbb.first_half_pace_ratio.label: Team first-half possession share and early-game pace ratio
cbb.first_half_pace_ratio.measurement: For each team compute r = (1H possessions)/(regulation possessions) per game from period box scores (possessions = FGA + 0.44*FTA - OREB + TO per half), averaged with half-life 15 games and shrunk to the league mean r_lg (about 0.485) with weight n/(n+12); expected 1H possessions = r_team_pair * expected regulation possessions where r_team_pair = average of the two teams' shrunk r; as-of: games before tip.
cbb.first_half_pace_ratio.mechanism: A team's first-half possessions as a share of its regulation possessions differ from 0.5 because second halves have more fouls and stoppages, and the size of the gap is team and coach specific.
cbb.first_half_pace_ratio.rationale: Scaling half possessions as half of the game's tempo mis-states the half total and half margin variance; teams that start slowly then accelerate are priced as if their pace were constant.
raw_data: per-half field-goal, free-throw, rebound and turnover counts

cbb.half_tie_probability.label: Integer pmf and tie probability of the half margin
cbb.half_tie_probability.measurement: Fit a discretized skew-normal or empirical-kernel model for the half margin with mean mu_h = 0.55*E[margin] and sd sigma_h = sqrt(poss_1H/34)*7.2, calibrated on at least 10 seasons of half margins; for tie, compute P(margin = 0) from the pmf with a correction factor c(|mu_h|) estimated from observed ties by expected-margin bucket (|mu| in 0-2, 2-5, 5-9, 9+); as-of: pregame mean and sd.
cbb.half_tie_probability.mechanism: The half margin is an integer with lumps of 1, 2 and 3 points, so its pmf has a central spike and parity structure that a normal density misses.
cbb.half_tie_probability.rationale: KXNCAAMB1H prices a tie as an outcome, and the 1H spread rungs near zero are also affected: each rung difference near 0 equals the pmf at one integer margin; mis-estimating the central mass by half a percentage point is a large error relative to the price.

cbb.halftime_state_adjustment.label: Halftime state update for second-half markets
cbb.halftime_state_adjustment.measurement: Regress second-half margin on pregame expected margin, 1H margin residual (1H margin minus 0.55*pregame expected), starters in foul trouble indicator (2+ fouls for a top-5 player), team foul counts, 1H 3P% minus expected, and an injury-in-game flag, using at least 5 seasons of halftime states; output conditional mean and sd of 2H margin and total (including OT mixture). Typical expected coefficient on the 1H residual: 0.1 to 0.25. Not available pregame; knowable at halftime.
cbb.halftime_state_adjustment.mechanism: Conditional on the first-half score, foul counts and shooting luck, the second-half margin and total have means shifted away from the pregame values by a small fraction of the first-half residual.
cbb.halftime_state_adjustment.rationale: The 2H series are live markets over the same game. The pregame prior plus an update on the halftime state is the correct information set, and the update is not 'trust the lead': most of a first-half lead is luck, but foul trouble and injuries are real.
raw_data: first-half score, fouls by player, shooting splits

cbb.handler_absence_pace_shift.label: With and without primary ball handler: pace and efficiency shift
cbb.handler_absence_pace_shift.measurement: For each team's top two ball handlers (highest assist-rate plus usage), estimate delta_poss = poss_per_40_off - poss_per_40_on and delta_ppp from on/off lineup splits over the last two seasons with ridge shrinkage lambda equal to 300 possessions off-court; scenario-weighted total shift = sum_k P(absent_k) * (delta_poss_k * ppp + poss * delta_ppp_k); as-of: lineup data through the previous game.
cbb.handler_absence_pace_shift.mechanism: A team's possessions per 40 and transition share change when its lead guard is off the floor, and its offensive efficiency changes more than defence.
cbb.handler_absence_pace_shift.rationale: Existing lineup inputs are labelled context and generic; the total contract needs the concrete delta in possessions and points per possession for the ball-handler absence scenario, weighted by the probability of that scenario.

cbb.implied_team_totals.label: Market-implied team points from spread and total
cbb.implied_team_totals.measurement: implied_home = (T - S)/2, implied_away = (T + S)/2 with S home spread; deviation from each team's rating-implied points; move since open.
cbb.implied_team_totals.mechanism: Spread and total jointly imply each team's expected points and thus possessions and efficiency for every player in the game.
cbb.implied_team_totals.rationale: Implied team total = (total +/- spread)/2; it moves with news before box-score features update, and summarizes the book's view of pace and scoring for this matchup.

As-of: format as announced before pricing.

cbb.incumbent_coach_departure_hazard.label: Incumbent head-coach departure hazard and succession arrangements
cbb.incumbent_coach_departure_hazard.measurement: For each sitting head coach at t: age, years remaining on contract, tenure, last three seasons' fundamentals-rating results versus preseason prior, conference and tournament results, reported health or retirement statements, announced coach-in-waiting or succession plan (flag with first report timestamp); hazard h(coach) = logistic fit of departure within 12 months on those covariates over at least 15 past seasons of all D1 head coaches, shrunk toward the age-band base rate with weight n/(n+25) coach-seasons; output P(vacancy opens before the cutoff date) and P(named successor already exists | vacancy).
cbb.incumbent_coach_departure_hazard.mechanism: A next-coach market can only pay out after a vacancy exists; before one does, the probability of any listed name is the probability of a vacancy before the cutoff times the conditional hire probability, and a pre-arranged coach-in-waiting changes the conditional distribution.
cbb.incumbent_coach_departure_hazard.rationale: For a template opened on a programme with a sitting coach, the dominant term is the chance the incumbent leaves (retirement, firing, a better job, health), driven by age, contract length, tenure, results against expectation and public succession statements. Subtle: retirements are lumpy around season ends and are often announced with a named successor, which concentrates mass on one name and removes the search entirely.
raw_data: coach-season table: school, coach, age, contract_end, tenure, departure flag and cause

cbb.interim_coach_season_audition.label: Interim coach's in-season audition: results versus preseason expectation and interim-to-permanent base rate
cbb.interim_coach_season_audition.measurement: For the interim coach at as-of t: games coached, AdjEM_fund results-versus-expectation = mean over games of (actual margin - cbb.ratings_fundamentals pregame expected margin), shrunk with weight n/(n+12) games toward 0; end-of-season gap between final fundamentals rating and the preseason prior from cbb.preseason_prior; projected conference finish and NCAA bid, seed and round-reached probabilities from cbb.bracket_sim; promotion base rate = share of past D1 interim or acting coaches who coached a full or most of a season (at least 15 games) and were then named permanent, split by whether the team met its preseason expectation (pooled over every available season, shrunk to the pooled mean with weight n/(n+8)); no betting line or price enters any term.
cbb.interim_coach_season_audition.mechanism: When an interim coaches the whole season before the search opens, the team's results under him are the main game-driven route to the permanent job: a clear beat of expectation, a conference finish above projection or an NCAA run turns the interim into a leading candidate or lets the school skip a search.
cbb.interim_coach_season_audition.rationale: Search timing and candidate ranking are set partly by what happens on the court during the deferred-search window. A promoted assistant inherits a roster chosen by the departed coach, so the fair comparison is results against a fundamentals-only expectation, not raw wins; a late-season run also raises the interim's profile with the AD and fan base. Subtle: interim promotions are rare enough that the base rate is tiny-sample, and a poor season can end the interim's case quickly.

cbb.joint_advancement_dependence.label: Dependence of two teams' tournament advancement (region, pod, avoidance rules)
cbb.joint_advancement_dependence.measurement: Simulate the bracket 50,000 times from the seed and region distribution (before Selection Sunday) or from the actual bracket (after): P(both reach R16) = joint frequency; also report the independence benchmark P_A*P_B and the ratio; the committee rule used is: same-conference teams avoided in rounds 1 and 2 where possible (verify yearly with the NCAA's principles and procedures document); as-of: bracket release.
cbb.joint_advancement_dependence.mechanism: Two teams' advancement probabilities are linked through the bracket: they cannot both advance if they meet, and share region and pod strength.
cbb.joint_advancement_dependence.rationale: KXNCAAMBBOTHQUAL asks for both teams in the Round of 16; the committee generally avoids same-conference matchups before the third round for teams of the same conference, but region and pod placement still matter and a correlation from correlated rating uncertainty exists.

cbb.kenpom_adjem_gap_density.label: KenPom AdjEM gap density around the target rank
cbb.kenpom_adjem_gap_density.measurement: At each daily snapshot sort AdjEM and compute for the target team gap_up = AdjEM(rank r-1) - AdjEM(team) and gap_down = AdjEM(team) - AdjEM(rank r+1), plus the number of teams within +/-0.5 AdjEM. Divide each gap by sigma_rel = sqrt(var_team + var_neighbour), where each team's variance to Mar 15 sums its own games_left times per-game update variance (cbb.kenpom_game_update_sensitivity), its season drift variance (cbb.kenpom_prior_drift) and an opponent re-adjustment term estimated from days without a game. For top-25 use the 25th-26th boundary. As-of: last snapshot before pricing.
cbb.kenpom_adjem_gap_density.mechanism: A rank contract is decided by the order statistics of ~360 AdjEM values; what matters is the AdjEM distance to the neighbouring ranks, not the absolute rating.
cbb.kenpom_adjem_gap_density.rationale: Near #25 teams are separated by a few tenths of a point of AdjEM while near #1 the gap can be a point or more, so identical rating noise moves a top-25 contract far more than a #1 contract. A team at #40 can be closer to the line in expected moves than a team at #28 if the intermediate teams are bunched.
raw_data: daily AdjEM for all D1 teams

cbb.kenpom_game_update_sensitivity.label: Per-game AdjEM update sensitivity
cbb.kenpom_game_update_sensitivity.measurement: Fit on daily snapshot pairs from the prior three seasons: dAdjEM_team,t = w(g) * (adjusted game margin per 100 possessions - AdjEM_t-1) + opponent-feedback term, with g games played; estimate w(g), a recency multiplier, and a blowout cap by least squares. Output expected move and sd per game as a function of g, opponent AdjEM and location. Validate: out-of-sample RMSE of next-day AdjEM below 0.15. As-of: snapshots before the game.
cbb.kenpom_game_update_sensitivity.mechanism: KenPom's rating is a running opponent-adjusted efficiency margin, so one game moves it by (game-level adjusted margin minus current rating) weighted by 1/games played, with opponent strength and venue entering the game-level number.
cbb.kenpom_game_update_sensitivity.rationale: A game's weight falls as games accumulate (assumed near 1/g, to be fitted), so a team moves about a point per game in November and a few tenths in March; the move is zero in expectation when the team performs at its rating. Recency and blowout treatment are not public, which is the subtle part.

cbb.kenpom_prior_drift.label: KenPom season-horizon rating drift and preseason-prior phase-out
cbb.kenpom_prior_drift.measurement: From stored daily ratings for the prior 5 seasons (KenPom archive if licensed, else Torvik T-Rank as proxy), compute D = AdjEM(Mar 15 equivalent: Monday after Selection Sunday) - AdjEM(d) per team for each pricing date d. Regress |D| and D on games remaining, preseason-prior weight at d (KenPom's stated phase-out, else estimated as the AdjEM gap between prior-inclusive and results-only ratings), returning-minutes share and transfer minutes (cbb.roster_minutes), own/opponent three-point luck (cbb.three_pt_luck) and schedule connectivity; output mean drift and sd per team-date, in AdjEM points per 100 possessions. As-of: ratings captured at d; no later revision used.
cbb.kenpom_prior_drift.mechanism: Between a November pricing date and Mar 15 a team's AdjEM moves because the preseason prior is phased out and its error revealed, and because true strength drifts with roster integration, injuries and shooting-luck regression.
cbb.kenpom_prior_drift.rationale: For most of the contract's life this variance, not the last week's games, decides rank probabilities. It is larger for high-churn rosters (low returning minutes, many transfers) and for teams with weakly connected schedules, and its expected sign can be predicted from three-point luck and the gap between prior and results-only ratings.

cbb.kenpom_rank_projection.label: Replication and projection of KenPom ratings to a timestamp
cbb.kenpom_rank_projection.measurement: Compute AdjO, AdjD and tempo by iterating opponent adjustment to convergence on all D1 games with venue factor 1.4 percent per side (approximate) and a decay weighting by game recency, calibrated so replicated AdjEM matches the KenPom value on historical snapshots with RMSE below 0.3 points; project to Mar 15 12:00 by simulating each remaining game (including conference tournaments) with the pairwise win and margin model, re-running the adjustment per simulated day, and recording rank distributions; as-of: simulation start date, cutoff time of the timestamp.
cbb.kenpom_rank_projection.mechanism: KenPom's rating is an opponent-adjusted efficiency margin computed from all completed games with venue and recency treatment, so the rank at a future time is a function of the results that will be counted before that time.
cbb.kenpom_rank_projection.rationale: KXNCAAMBKENPOMRANK and KXNCAAMBKENPOMTOP settle on a snapshot list; the uncertainty is the future results and the rating algorithm, not human opinion, so a faithful replication (with game-by-game updates) is the only way to evaluate crowded ranks.

cbb.leader_average_inertia.label: Leaderboard average inertia and remaining-swing bound
cbb.leader_average_inertia.measurement: For each pair (leader, challenger) compute the gap in current average, the number of games remaining for each (regular-season schedule plus expected postseason), the per-game sd, and the swing bound d = (mu_challenger - mu_leader) * G_rem/(g+G_rem) plus the standard error sqrt(G_rem) * sd/(g+G_rem). The feature is z = (gap - expected_catch_up)/se. As-of: updated after every game by either player.
cbb.leader_average_inertia.mechanism: A season average changes by exactly (x - mean)/(g+1) after a game with value x, so the games remaining limit how far the gap between the leader and challengers can close, and late in the season a lead is close to locked.
cbb.leader_average_inertia.rationale: At 25 games played one 40-point game raises a 20 ppg average by under 0.8, and a challenger 1.5 ppg back needs several far above average games, so the effective uncertainty falls as 1/g; postseason games add few extra samples, which matters most for players on deep-tournament teams.

cbb.league_scoring_baseline_drift.label: League-wide scoring baseline and rule-emphasis drift
cbb.league_scoring_baseline_drift.measurement: league_ppp_t = EWMA over the last 14 days of league-wide points per 100 possessions across all D1 games with half-life 21 days, plus an indicator for a rule-emphasis change flagged by NCAA rules committee announcements; expected total = sum of team unit ratings (relative) + 2 * league_ppp_t * expected_poss / 100; stored with timestamp so it uses only games completed before tip.
cbb.league_scoring_baseline_drift.mechanism: The national points-per-100 baseline changes by month (non-conference to conference play) and across seasons with rule emphasis, shot clock and officiating mandates.
cbb.league_scoring_baseline_drift.rationale: Adjusted ratings are relative to an average opponent; absolute totals depend on the current league mean, which moves several points per game between November and March and between rule years, and shifts early before ratings catch up.

cbb.live_game_state_tie_path.label: Live score, clock, period, possession and foul state for in-play overtime pricing
cbb.live_game_state_tie_path.measurement: At as-of t during the game: period, seconds remaining, score margin, possession, team fouls and bonus status for both teams, count of players with 4 fouls and fouled-out players, OT index k already played; P(rung N | state) = P(tie at end of current period | state) x P_tie_OT^(N-k-1) using a state-based first-passage model on the margin (fit on play-by-play with state buckets: margin -6..+6, clock 60 s bins in the last 5 minutes); record feed latency (seconds from event to capture) and discard states older than the latency budget.
cbb.live_game_state_tie_path.mechanism: Once a game is close late or in overtime, the rung probability is set by the current score difference, time left, possession, team-foul bonus status and players near five fouls, and the pregame margin model becomes nearly irrelevant.
cbb.live_game_state_tie_path.rationale: The 2+ and 3+ rungs sit near zero until regulation is tied or in extra time; if the market trades during the game, almost all price movement comes from the live state. Subtle: a tie at the final buzzer needs both possession and timing, and an overtime already in progress changes the remaining number of required ties by one for each rung; free live feeds can lag, so the data latency itself is a modelling input.
raw_data: live play-by-play: timestamp, period, clock, score, possession, team fouls, player fouls
capture-time stamps to measure feed latency

cbb.margin_regime_mixture.label: Competitive versus blowout regime mixture of the final margin
cbb.margin_regime_mixture.measurement: Fit on historical closing-line-independent model expected margins m_hat: P(blowout)=logistic(a + b*|m_hat| + c*coach_decay) with a normal-in-regime margin for each regime (mu_k, sd_k) and a discrete overtime spike mass at margins 1 to 6 whose weight equals P(tie at 0:00) from the ot model; output the integer-margin pmf (for strikes at .5 and win-margin buckets) at pregame as-of; refit each season with at least 10 prior seasons.
cbb.margin_regime_mixture.mechanism: Final margin is a mixture of a competitive regime (late fouling, overtime) and a blowout regime (compressed, coach-dependent), with the mixing weight a threshold function of the expected margin.
cbb.margin_regime_mixture.rationale: A single normal with sd 10 mis-prices tails at both ends: too fat in the blowout regime for favourites covering large numbers, and too thin right at tied-game and overtime-driven 1 to 5 point margins. Winning-margin buckets and 40+ point spreads sit in exactly these regimes.
raw_data: historical final scores with OT flag
pregame expected margin per game (model output)

cbb.margin_total_covariance.label: Joint distribution of margin and total for same-game parlays
cbb.margin_total_covariance.measurement: Estimate corr(margin_resid, total_resid) from standardized residuals (actual minus model expectation, divided by game-level sd) bucketed by favourite size (0-5, 5-10, 10-20, 20+) and by team tempo tercile, with shrinkage to the pooled correlation weight n/(n+200) per bucket; as-of all prior games; apply through a bivariate normal copula with the regime mixture margins.
cbb.margin_total_covariance.mechanism: Margin and total are not independent: tempo and scoring-environment shocks move both teams' points together while blowouts reshape both margin and total through bench play and clock use.
cbb.margin_total_covariance.rationale: KXNCAAMBSGP is a conjunction of a spread cover and a total; pricing it as the product of two marginals mis-prices a systematic correlation, typically positive for favourites in fast games (favourite scores more, total higher) and negative when a slow favourite grinds.
raw_data: historical final score for both teams per game
pregame expected margin and expected total from the model

free_sources: Derived from bracket simulation and player models
cbb.milestone_union_aggregation.label: Any-player union over all tournament player-games with dependence
cbb.milestone_union_aggregation.measurement: Monte Carlo: simulate the bracket (with First Four) N >= 50,000 times; for each simulated game draw active players' stat lines from their per-game models (minutes linked to game margin and OT); YES if any line hits the milestone; report P(YES) and the contribution share of the top 10 players; compare with the analytical 1 - prod(1 - p_i)^{E[games_i]} as a check.
cbb.milestone_union_aggregation.mechanism: YES = at least one player-game hits the milestone; probability is one minus the probability that none does, computed over correlated player-games in a bracket where survival paths are shared.
cbb.milestone_union_aggregation.rationale: Simple independence summation overstates YES when probability is concentrated on a few stars whose games are correlated by team survival, and the chance that a candidate's team loses early removes several of his games at once. Subtle: the event is dominated by a handful of players, so the union is sensitive to errors in their tails, and 'long tail' depth (many players at very small probabilities) still contributes.

cbb.minutes_scenario_mixture.label: Minutes scenario mixture by game state and foul risk
cbb.minutes_scenario_mixture.measurement: Fit for each player-role bucket (starter guard, starter wing, starter big, rotation) a three-component model on minutes: component weights w_k = softmax(a_k + b_k*|expected margin| + c_k*foul_rate_per_40 + d_k*back-to-back flag), with component means estimated from last two seasons of games per coach with ridge shrinkage; output the pmf over minutes in 4-minute bins; as-of: spread-free (use model expected margin, not market line).
cbb.minutes_scenario_mixture.mechanism: A player's minutes are a mixture of at least three regimes (competitive full minutes, blowout truncated, foul-trouble truncated) with weights set by the spread, the coach's rotation habits and the foul propensity.
cbb.minutes_scenario_mixture.rationale: A single expected-minutes number averages a bimodal variable; for a star on a 15-point favourite the 28-minute mode and the 34-minute mode generate very different probabilities of reaching 25 points, so the mixture matters more for high rungs than for the median.
raw_data: final margin and pregame expected margin

cbb.miss_location_mix.label: Expected location mix of missed shots (rim, mid-range, three) and perimeter rebound share
cbb.miss_location_mix.measurement: For game g, expected misses by zone M_z = sum over both teams of FGA_z * (1 - make_z) using team shot mix and opponent-adjusted zone make rates; perimeter share of rebounds by position from historical play-by-play: P(guard collects | three-point miss) and P(big collects | rim miss) with shrinkage; player-level adjustment: expected rebounds = sum_z M_z * share_player,z shrunk toward the position mean with n/(n+300). As-of: shot mix over the last 15 games.
cbb.miss_location_mix.mechanism: Long misses from three-point shots produce longer rebounds that go to guards and wings more often, while rim misses go to bigs; a team's shot mix therefore reallocates the rebound pool among positions.
cbb.miss_location_mix.rationale: A guard's rebound line looks high in games where both teams shoot many threes and low against a rim-oriented opponent; position-blind pool totals miss this reallocation.
raw_data: team shot attempts and makes by zone
rebound events with rebounder and shot type

cbb.number_one_transition_model.label: Markov model of the #1 holder and successor distribution after a loss
cbb.number_one_transition_model.measurement: State: current #1, set of previous #1s, week t (1 to 19). Transition: P(change in week t) = 1 - (1 - L_t) where L_t = prob #1 loses in the week plus P(leapfrog without a loss) estimated from AP archives 2000 to 2026 (leapfrog rate about 3 to 8 percent per week, to be fitted); successor chosen by softmax over the top-8 contenders with features (poll points gap, record, rating gap, unbeaten flag) fitted on past changes; count distinct holders via Monte Carlo of 20,000 seasons using game-by-game loss probabilities from the ratings of the top teams; as-of: latest poll and schedule.
cbb.number_one_transition_model.mechanism: The distinct-#1 count is 1 plus the number of changes at the top in which the new holder has not been #1 before; changes occur when the current #1 loses (or is leapfrogged) and the successor is drawn from the contenders.
cbb.number_one_transition_model.rationale: A threshold such as 9 distinct #1 teams is far into the tail of a process whose typical value is 3 to 6 (to be computed from AP archives, not asserted), so the tail depends on the weekly leapfrog probability and on how often the successor is a new team; neither is a function of ratings alone.
raw_data: weekly AP poll top 8 with points

cbb.opp_foul_propensity_ft_points.label: Opponent foul propensity converted to the team's expected free-throw points

cbb.opp_foul_propensity_ft_points.rationale: Free-throw points are a high-leverage part of a team total because they cost no clock; the opponent's foul rate is a stable team trait (pressure man defence or hand-checking) that the existing free-throw input measures only for the named team.

officials crew for the game (if known)

cbb.opp_three_defense_persistence_split.label: Opponent three-point defence: persistent attempts conceded versus non-persistent percentage allowed

cbb.opp_three_defense_persistence_split.mechanism: A defence's scheme controls the number of threes it concedes, a persistent trait, while the percentage opponents make against it is largely noise.
cbb.opp_three_defense_persistence_split.rationale: Opponent allowed 3P% is routinely used as a matchup input but is mostly luck and should be shrunk almost entirely to the league mean, while the attempt-conceded rate retains most of its signal.

cbb.ot_foul_carryover_depletion.label: Player-foul and team-foul carryover into overtime and resulting lineup depletion
cbb.ot_foul_carryover_depletion.measurement: Rule version assumed (unverified for 2026-27, see ot_u3): men's two 20-minute halves, five personal fouls to disqualify, team-foul bonus carrying from the second half into overtime periods, five-minute overtimes; store a rule_version flag per game and fit only on seasons with the same structure. From play-by-play for all OT games: at the start of each OT period, count players with 4 and 5 fouls per team (weighted by their minutes share), team-foul count and bonus status; points per team per OT period and distribution of scoring events by value; estimate P(tie after OT k | depletion state) by logistic fit pooled over 10 seasons; pregame proxy = team foul rate and bench depth.
cbb.ot_foul_carryover_depletion.mechanism: Player fouls and second-half team fouls carry into overtime, so teams entering OT have players near or at the five-foul limit and are already in the bonus, changing scoring variance in each five-minute period.
cbb.ot_foul_carryover_depletion.rationale: Repeat ties depend on how many points are scored per OT period and how lumpy they are: bonus free throws add frequent one- and two-point scores, and fouled-out starters lower efficiency unevenly. Subtle: the carryover makes later OT periods progressively more foul-driven, so per-period tie probability is not constant across periods.

cbb.ot_model.label: Overtime probability and extra-period scoring
cbb.ot_model.measurement: Empirical OT frequency by closing spread and total bucket; expected OT points per team; match to rules_text inclusion.
cbb.ot_model.mechanism: Regulation ties lead to 5-minute overtimes that add roughly 8-10 points to totals and affect OT-inclusive settlement.
cbb.ot_model.rationale: CBB overtime frequency is a few percent of games; late fouling by the trailing team shifts the distribution of margins. OT matters for totals, spreads and player props when included in settlement and not at all when excluded. Subtle: more fouls late means more free throws, so P(tie at end of regulation) is not independent of FT%.

cbb.ot_period_tie_chain.label: Overtime reach and repeat-tie chain
cbb.ot_period_tie_chain.measurement: P_tie_reg = integer pmf at margin 0 from the game's margin distribution (normal with sd = sqrt(poss/68)*10.5, centred at the model expected margin, with a discrete correction for the fact that tied scores cluster at lower margins); P_tie_OT = empirical rate of tied-after-OT among all OT periods over the last 10 seasons (per period, shrunk by count), with a multiplier for two-team free-throw rate; P(N+ periods) = P_tie_reg * P_tie_OT^(N-1); extra points per OT period = empirical mean (about 10 to 12 combined) with sd. As-of: pregame expected margin and total.
cbb.ot_period_tie_chain.mechanism: P(OT) is the probability of a tie at the end of regulation (a function of expected margin, total and variance); each additional period needs another tie, with per-period tie probability set by five-minute scoring variance and fouling.
cbb.ot_period_tie_chain.rationale: KXNCAAMBOT prices counts like 3+ periods, which need P(OT) times two repeat ties, a probability of order 0.1 percent that no ordinary total or margin model produces correctly. The same chain defines the right-tail mass of the points total.

cbb.pace_elasticity_to_opponent.label: Team pace elasticity to opponent tempo
cbb.pace_elasticity_to_opponent.measurement: For each team over the last two seasons regress game possessions on own adjusted tempo and opponent adjusted tempo (opponent-adjusted, centred on league mean): poss = a + b_own*(T_own - T_lg) + b_opp*(T_opp - T_lg); estimate b_own and b_opp per team with ridge shrinkage toward league coefficients (lambda equivalent to 12 games); expected game possessions for a matchup = league mean + b_own_A*(T_A - lg) + b_opp_A*(T_B - lg), averaged with the same computed from team B's coefficients, weights proportional to inverse variance. As-of: games completed before the prior day.
cbb.pace_elasticity_to_opponent.mechanism: A team's realised possessions respond to opponent tempo with a team-specific slope: dictators hold their own pace, adapters match the opponent.
cbb.pace_elasticity_to_opponent.rationale: The shared possession count is where own-team scoring volume comes from. Using the average of two tempos assumes a common 0.5 weight, which is wrong for many pairs and shifts a team's expected total by 2 to 4 points.
raw_data: both teams' season-to-date adjusted tempo before each game

cbb.player_foul.label: Player foul rate and foul-trouble minute risk
cbb.player_foul.measurement: PF per 40, P(2+ first-half fouls) and P(foul-out) from game logs; opponent foul-drawing rate; coach benching rule.
cbb.player_foul.mechanism: Players with high foul rates are benched or foul out, truncating minutes and counting stats, especially bigs.
cbb.player_foul.rationale: Foul trouble creates left-tail outcomes for props; the risk depends on baseline fouls per 40, opponent foul-drawing, and officiating. Coaches differ in how early they bench players. Subtle: first-half foul trouble affects first-half markets differently from full-game markets.

cbb.player_ft_trips_xfta.label: Player expected free-throw attempts: drawn-foul rate and late-game ball-handling share
cbb.player_ft_trips_xfta.measurement: xFTA = (drawn-foul FTA rate per 100 on-court possessions, last 20 games, half-life 10, shrunk n/(n+8) to role mean) * expected on-court possessions + P(close at 2:00 left) * (ball-handler share of late possessions) * expected late FTA per team (about 4 in a one-possession game); FT% enters separately with shrinkage n/(n+100) to 72 percent league mean; as-of: pregame.
cbb.player_ft_trips_xfta.mechanism: Player FTA equal drawn fouls per 100 possessions times possessions on court times a bonus factor, plus a late-game component for ball handlers on teams likely to lead or to be fouled at the end.
cbb.player_ft_trips_xfta.rationale: Free throws are a distinct scoring channel with its own distribution; late-game trips depend on the probability of a close game and on who handles the ball, so guards and wings differ even at equal usage.
raw_data: player FTA per game with minutes

cbb.player_game_exposure_tournament.label: Expected tournament games per candidate player (field entry x team survival x availability)
cbb.player_game_exposure_tournament.measurement: For each player as of t: E[games] = sum_r P(team bid) * P(team plays round r | bid) * P(player active in r), using the bracket simulation with fundamentals-only ratings; P(active) from injury status and star injury risk; before Selection Sunday include bid probability; report full distribution of games (1 to 7, or more under an expanded field). In-tournament state: after the field is set, condition on the live bracket at t (teams still alive, games already played, results to date) and set P(YES) = 1 for the relevant series once any qualifying game is final; remaining exposure = games still to be played by surviving teams only.
cbb.player_game_exposure_tournament.mechanism: A player can only hit a milestone in games his team plays; expected exposure is the sum over rounds of P(team in field) times P(team reaches that round) times P(player active).
cbb.player_game_exposure_tournament.rationale: Total team-games in the tournament are fixed by the format, but they concentrate on strong teams; a star on a 1 seed averages several games, a star on a 16 seed one or two. Subtle: the First Four counts, so play-in teams add a game, and a changed field size changes the count. The market trades through the tournament window, so exposure must be recomputed as teams are eliminated and as a milestone either occurs (settling YES) or becomes unreachable with fewer games left.
raw_data: bracket simulation output: team, round, probability

cbb.player_points_dispersion_by_role.label: Player points dispersion index by role
cbb.player_points_dispersion_by_role.measurement: For each role bucket compute phi = var(points | minutes bucket, expected usage) / mean over the last 3 seasons of player games with weight to the player's own phi_i = n/(n+25) shrinkage; use negative binomial with mean mu and size r = mu/(phi-1) conditional on playing 15+ minutes, mixed with the DNP point mass; output per-rung probabilities; as-of: pregame.
cbb.player_points_dispersion_by_role.mechanism: Variance of a player's single-game points relative to his mean varies by role (high-usage guard versus low-usage big) and by shot mix.
cbb.player_points_dispersion_by_role.rationale: High rungs (25 plus) read the tail of the count distribution, and the tail width depends on role variance more than on the mean; using one dispersion for all players mis-prices the high and low rungs in opposite directions.
raw_data: player points per game with minutes

cbb.player_scoring_tail_index.label: Player single-game scoring right-tail index (probability of 40+ and 50+ point games)
cbb.player_scoring_tail_index.measurement: Per player: fit a compound model points = minutes x usage-based attempts x points per attempt with Beta-uncertain shooting and NB attempt dispersion, on the last 2 seasons of game logs; validate tail mass against observed 35+/40+ frequencies of D1 players pooled by role (generalised Pareto fit above 30 points, threshold chosen by mean-excess plot); output P(points >= 50 | game played) with credible interval. Attempt volume is scaled by the ratio of matchup expected possessions (cbb.tempo) to the possessions of the player's logged games.
cbb.player_scoring_tail_index.mechanism: A 50-point game sits far beyond typical college means, so its probability depends on the right tail of the player's game scoring distribution, driven by volume ceiling (shot attempts, free-throw trips) and hot shooting.
cbb.player_scoring_tail_index.rationale: Mean and sd from a negative binomial understate extreme tails for high-usage shooters and overstate them for efficient interior scorers. Subtle: extreme games usually combine high attempts, a hot three-point night and extra minutes (overtime), so the tail is a compound of several stages, not a single scale parameter.
raw_data: player game logs: minutes, FGA, 3PA, FTA, points

cbb.possession_length_profile.rationale: A single adjusted tempo hides the matchup: a team that attacks early facing a defence that forces shot-clock-long possessions plays slower than the average of tempos suggests; this is the first-order total driver, since a three-possession error is about three to four points of total.
raw_data: team season-to-date average possession length offence and defence
